selection.reason: The rear position, stop and reversing functions fall within this consolidated regulation, including applicable photometric and colour requirements for the assembled lamps and their outer lens.
The integrated moulded-prism retro-reflector is a retro-reflective device covered by this consolidated regulation.
Installation on the M1 passenger car must satisfy the positioning, geometric visibility, orientation and operating requirements for the rear position, stop and reversing lamps and retro-reflector.
The LED modules and PCB constitute electrical/electronic equipment whose electromagnetic emissions and immunity must be addressed at component or vehicle-integration level.
The externally mounted lens and housing must satisfy applicable M1 external-projection requirements concerning exposed edges, projections and surface geometry.
Integration of the stop-lamp function with the M1 braking system must respect the requirements governing generation of the signal that illuminates the stop lamps.
The rear lamp's installation must support continued correct operation and visibility of its lighting and signalling functions following the prescribed low-speed rear protective-device impact tests.
Its rear position and stop-lamp provisions are consolidated into UN R148, which is selected instead.
Its reversing-lamp provisions are consolidated into UN R148, which is selected instead.
Its retro-reflector provisions are consolidated into UN R150, which is selected instead.
The specification identifies LED modules on a PCB, not a standardised LED light-source category covered by Annex 1, so separate approval under this regulation is not established.
Its scope expressly excludes glazing for lighting and light-signalling devices, including this lamp's PMMA outer lens.
